sources.source_title: Amana Solid Carbide Spektra Spiral Plunge 2/3 Flute Chart v24
sources.coverage_notes: Flat/compression wood tooling feed and chipload chart. Smallest diameters: 1/32" (0.794mm), 1.5mm. Chart covers Wood/Plywood and MDF/Laminate columns; does NOT cover ball nose or tapered ball nose tools (these are flat/compression spirals only). Chart does NOT separate softwood from hardwood. The chart prints ONE chip load per tooth per diameter (no range), no finish rows and no ap or ae range; its only depth statement is 1 x D plus the feed de-rate (2 x D -25%, 3 x D -50%). Since 2026-09-23 (feeds matrix R5): the 14 amana_flat_end.json rows that cite this chart but are not printed on it (ranges, hardwood/HDF/particleboard splits, a contour finish row, ap ranges such as 0.5xD to 1.5xD) carry row_kind derived, evidence_grade c and a notes field; the printed 2F and 3F rows at 1/8", 6mm and 1/4" are bundled in amana_flat_end.json in the pocket and adaptive families, as exact grade a for MDF/Laminate and as derived grade b for the four wood and plywood families that share the one Wood/Plywood column. Single values are encoded as chipload_max_mm_tooth only.

sources.source_title: Amana Spiral Ball Nose Speed Chart v7
sources.coverage_notes: Ball nose chart rows for wood, MDF, plastic, and aluminum. Smallest diameter covered: 1/16" (1.587mm). Chart values are calibrated for 1xD-depth slot/peripheral cutting, NOT 3D parallel finishing — using these CPT values as 3D-finish bounds would be aggressive. The 3.175mm and 6mm parallel/scallop rows first bundled in this file are derived (reduced, about x0.16 to x0.26 of the printed midpoint, no named source) for 3D-finish use; since 2026-09-23 (feeds matrix R5) they carry row_kind derived, evidence_grade c and a notes field that names the factor. The printed 1/8" and 1/4" Hardwood, Softwood and MDF rows are bundled as exact grade a rows (amana-ball-*-v7) in the pocket and adaptive families with pass_role roughing, so finish queries keep the derived rows; sub-1mm rows from this chart are NOT transcribed for the same reason. Coverage gap: no sub-1mm 3D-finish-calibrated ball nose rows; use amana_zrn_3d_profiling instead.

sources.source_title: Amana ZrN 3D Profiling Feed and Chip Load Chart
sources.coverage_notes: Ball/tapered-ball/flat profiling guidance. Diameters covered: 1/32" (0.794mm), 1mm, 1.5mm, 1/16" (1.587mm), 1/8" (3.175mm), 3/16" (4.762mm), 6mm, 1/4", 3/8", 1/2". COVERAGE GAP: chart conflates softwood/hardwood/MDF/sign-foam under one 'Wood, MDF, Sign-Foam' row — does NOT separate softwood from hardwood at any diameter. Sub-1mm rows added 2026-05-02 (1mm 2-flute, 1/16" 2-flute, 1/32" 3-flute, 1.5mm 4-flute) are emitted as softwood and MDF only; HARDWOOD AT SUB-1MM IS A DOCUMENTED GAP — vendor's wood data is not split, and per refusal-first we do not invent reduced-CPT hardwood rows. The chart's printed CPT for 2-flute 1/16" Wood (0.003-0.005 inch) is INCONSISTENT with the printed IPM (55-90 IPM at 18000 RPM 2-flute → 0.00153-0.0025 inch); the 1/16" 2-flute row in observations uses the IPM-derived value and is marked row_kind='derived'.

sources.source_title: Onsrud Cutting Data Recommendations
sources.coverage_notes: Router guidance across wood/plastic/aluminum families. Per-material PDFs (Hard Wood, Soft Wood, MDF) reviewed 2026-05-02. Smallest diameter in any of those PDFs is 1/16" (1.587mm) and only on series 64-000/65-000 (downcut spiral / compression spiral — flat-end, NOT ball nose). CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (feeds matrix R5): the Hard Wood, Soft Wood, MDF and Hard Plywood PDFs DO print a tapered ball series, 77-100 (1/8 in .003-.005, 1/4 in .005-.007 in/tooth, 1 x D); the Soft Plywood PDF does not. These rows are bundled in onsrud_tapered_ball.json. The PDFs print no plain ball nose and no sub-1mm tapered entry; for ball/tapered-ball sub-1mm coverage, Amana ZrN 3D Profiling is the only public vendor source we have. This index page prints no bull, corner-radius or radius series; the four onsrud-bull-* rows that cite it are derived grade c since 2026-09-23 (see their notes).

The APPLICATION table names 60-200 for finishing but the chip-load table prints no 60-200 row, and the sheet prints no 77-100 row; neither is transcribed. The chip-load table has no 3/32 in column. One printed line is NOT bundled: 60-100MW 1/8 in .013-.015 in/tooth (0.330-0.381 mm) reaches 0.12 x D, the loader plausibility ceiling (validate_observation rule 5), so the row is left out and the soft plywood 1/8 in contour query borrows the hard plywood row. Depth rule as printed: 1 x D recommended chip load; 2 x D reduce chip load by 25%; 3 x D reduce chip load by 50%.

sources.source_title: Garr Tool Milling Guide for Aluminum (Low-Range HP/Torque) Series 242M/842M/A3 End Mills
sources.coverage_notes: Bundled 2026-05-31 (Phase B of completion plan). Low-Range page of Garr's three-page Aluminum Milling Guide. Chart presents one chipload triplet shared across series 242M (2-flute) / 842M (2-flute) / A3 (3-flute); promoted as 9 per-series rows (3 chart entries × 3 series) so per-flute matching gates can dispatch correctly. Diameters covered: 3.0 mm and 6.0 mm; operations slotting (pocket) and profiling (contour). Verbatim metric chiploads from the chart's M/Min table — no inch round-trip. Excluded from this promotion: Mid-Range (142M/143M) and General-Purpose rows — neither had pre-authorized flute counts. See planning/feeds_data_ingest_phaseB_2026-05-31.md.

A3 series only (3-flute, aerospace-grade); no per-series split needed. 2 rows: HEM profiling (adaptive/roughing, 6 mm, CPT 0.120–0.180 mm/tooth) and finishing (contour/finish, 6 mm, CPT 0.060 mm/tooth single value). sources.source_title: Garr Tool General Purpose Milling Chart — Aluminum Section
sources.coverage_notes: Bundled 2026-06-01 (Phase 4 + Phase 5 Step 5.3). General-Purpose milling chart: 2 aluminum rows (3 mm and 6 mm, 2-flute) + 1 fiberglass / G10 / composite-non-ISO row (6 mm 2-flute, CPT 0.030–0.051 mm/tooth, SMM 79–157 m/min). The composite row was deferred during Phase 4 (material_family='plastic' was not a valid MaterialFamily variant) and landed in Phase 5 Step 5.3 after `MaterialFamily::Fiberglass` and `Material::Fiberglass { grade }` were added (see planning/phase_5_schema_unlock_2026-06-01.md). Garr's chart collapses Fiberglass + Plastics + G10 onto one row; the promoted observation uses material_family='fiberglass' because the abrasive + fiber-reinforced cutting class dominates the envelope — promoting only the high-confidence interpretation. Plastic-only chiploads for HDPE/Acrylic/Delrin/etc. are NOT inferred from this row; they should source from polymer-specific vendor charts.

sources.source_title: USDA Forest Service, Wood Handbook — Wood as an Engineering Material, GTR FPL-GTR-190 (2010), Chapter 5 'Mechanical Properties of Wood' by David E. Kretschmann, Table 5-3a
sources.coverage_notes: Phase E (completion plan, 2026-05-31): peer-reviewed Janka side-hardness for ~98 wood species, used as the primary source for `Material::SolidWoodByJanka` library entries via `WOOD_SPECIES_LIBRARY`. Janka values converted from the published Newton column (Table 5-3a 'Side hardness') by `lbf = N / 4.448` rounded to 1 decimal. The 'Green' moisture rows are excluded — only the 12% MC line (kiln-dried, typical workshop stock) is staged. Primary `fpl.fs.usda.gov` URL 403'd on 2026-05-30; the precisebits.com mirror serves the identical 46-page PDF. Touches no live vendor LUT rows — wood Kc lookups remain driven by the in-crate Janka → Kc helper, not by LUT row matching.

sources.source_title: LMT Onsrud Article: Routing Polycarbonate Material
sources.coverage_notes: Bundled 2026-06-01 (Phase 5 Step 5.2 — V-bit schema relaxation). Article publishes a diameter-independent chipload window (0.004-0.012 in/tooth = 0.1016-0.3048 mm/tooth) for upcut O-flute routing of polycarbonate, plus operational guidance (side-entry / ramp required, no straight plunge). One observation row, `diameter_mm` omitted (None) — matched by tool_family + material + operation.

sources.source_title: The Wood Database (https://www.wood-database.com/) — per-species Janka hardness pages, 2026-05-30 snapshot
sources.coverage_notes: Phase E (completion plan, 2026-05-31): single-source per-species Janka pages for ~34 species that FPL Ch.5 Table 5-3a does not cover (typically tropical / specialty species the Wood Database does cover individually). Used as fill-in for `WOOD_SPECIES_LIBRARY` after FPL precedence — entries that appear in both sources prefer the FPL value. Verbatim quote convention: 'Janka Hardness: {N,NNN} lbf ({N,NNN} N)' per the wood-database article on Janka methodology.
